dva-avc-107.text: A company wants to allow users of IAM perform operations NORMAIS day-to-day (read access to most resources) without MFA, but require that any attempt to perform operations DESTRUTIVAS (ex.: 'ec2:Termination', 'dynamodb:DeleteTable') be NEGADA, unless the user's session has been established COM MFA (that is, the user authenticated using a device MFA physical/virtual when obtaining your session credentials). dva-avc-108.text: A team has a backend application SERVER-SIDE (performing in a safe environment, e.g. a task of ECS, able to protect a secret value) that needs to authenticate users against a Cognito User Pool calling 'InitiateAuth' with 'USER_PASSWORD_AUTH'. The team created the APP CLIENT User Pool with 'Generate Secret Client' HABILITADO (a confidential client). Calls to 'InitiateAuth' from this backend are failing with an error indicating an missing parameter, even with correct user and password. What additional parameter should the backend include in 'AuthParameters'?
options: 'SECRET_HASH' — when a client app is configured COM a secret client (a 'confidential client'), every call from API authentication (e.g. 'InitiateAuth', 'RespondToAuthChallenge', 'SignUp') must include a value 'SECRET_HASH' in the parameters — this is a hash HMAC-SHA256 calculated from the username (or other relevant value), the client app ID and the client app secret client; Cognito uses this to verify that the caller application has the secret client. Public clients (without secret) do not need this parameter, but confidential clients (with secret enabled) always need.
'DEVICE_KEY' — device identifier used by device tracking feature of Cognito.
'REFRESH_TOKEN' — token used to get new access/ID tokens without re-authenticating with user and password.
'CLIENT_SECRET' — the client's secret client's literal value should be included directly in 'AuthParameters''.
dva-avc-108.explanation: Correct. When the client app from Cognito has a secret client enabled, all calls from API authentication require parameter 'SECRET_HASH', one HMAC-SHA256 derived from the username, the ID client and the secret client. Without this parameter, called 'InitiateAuth' fail with an error of missing parameter — exactly the symptom described.
dva-avc-108.hint: Think about what a client app from Cognito configured COM secret client requires in every authentication call, derived from secret client but without exposing the secret itself.
optionRationales: Correct. When the client app from Cognito has a secret client enabled, all calls from API authentication require parameter 'SECRET_HASH', one HMAC-SHA256 derived from the username, the ID client and the secret client. Without this parameter, called 'InitiateAuth' fail with an error of missing parameter — exactly the symptom described.

Incorrect. Although the client app TENHA a secret client value, the authentication APIs of the Cognito do not accept a parameter 'CLIENT_SECRET' raw in 'AuthParameters' for security reasons (this exposed the secret in parameters/logs of calls from API) — instead, the application must calculate and send the 'SECRET_HASH' (one HMAC derived from secrecy), never the secret itself.

Incorrect. 'DEVICE_KEY' is used by the RASTREAMENTO OF DISPOSITIVOS/memory of devices from Cognito (identifying a previously recognized specific device of a user, e.g.: to jump MFA on reliable devices) — is not related to whether the client app has a secret client, and is not the missing parameter for the basic authentication call of a confidential client.

Incorrect. 'REFRESH_TOKEN' is used as a parameter of authentication flow 'REFRESH_TOKEN_AUTH' (to get new tokens using a previously issued token refresh), not for the initial flow 'USER_PASSWORD_AUTH' with user/password — is not related to the secret client requirement described.
